stories.headline: WIRE review recovery gets an exact attestation workstream, but queue validation fails
stories.summary: A narrowly scoped implementation and independent-review pair now exists to authenticate WIRE exporter's preserved review source. Automatic handoff promoted both packets, but repository queue-authority validation and a subsequent handoff run failed. No attestation implementation, independent PASS, or transport delivery is established.
stories.body:
A new exact-source-attestation implementation/review pair was authored at 834341ab and promoted at 0e5da248. It targets the preserved exporter-review host-validation refusal, binding the proposed exception to specific source and manifest blobs, archived packet identity, reviewed main, and review run. The correction must remain inert until its own independent review is accepted.

GitHub Actions show Automatic Packet Authoring Handoff succeeded for the authored pair, but Validate Repository failed at the queue-authority gate. A subsequent handoff run on the promotion commit also failed its 'Validate and publish explicitly authorized pairs' step. These are separate failures and cannot be assumed to have the same cause. Promotion on main is not proof that the live dispatcher considers either packet claimable.

The original exporter remains landed and its preserved review is not accepted. The transport implementation/review pair remains dependency-gated; no private Dropbox observation or ChatGPT consumer readback is verified. Host worktree, lock, process and disk status were not freshly inspected.
bullets: Exact-source-attestation implementation/review pair authored and promoted on main.
New correction is designed to remain inert until its own genuine independent PASS.
Repository queue-authority validation failed on authoring commit.
Subsequent automatic handoff failed on promotion commit; eligibility is not established.
Exporter review and dependent private transport remain blocked.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has published a targeted recovery path for WIRE's stalled independent review. The new workstream aims to prove exactly which exporter source and validation-manifest change the reviewer may trust. Its packet handoff advanced, but two CI checks failed, so this is authorization groundwork, not a recovered review.

sections.heading: A recovery bound to one source
sections.text: The new packet specifies exact implementation, archive, merge, manifest and preserved-review identities. Its proposed attestation cannot activate merely because code lands: it must pass its own independent review. That narrow scope is intended to unblock the original exporter review without weakening unrelated review safeguards.

sections.heading: Promotion does not erase failed checks
sections.text: The authoring handoff succeeded and promoted both packets to ready/auto in repository text. However, repository validation failed the queue-authority step, and a later automatic handoff failed on the promoted commit. Their precise causes require investigation; neither failure proves the attestation logic itself is defective.

sections.heading: The operational WIRE remains offline
sections.text: The exporter is landed, but its independent review has no accepted verdict. The private transport is still dependency-gated. Until review acceptance, transport implementation, and verified private retrieval occur, WIRE cannot present live dispatcher measurements.

insights.title: The missing evidence now has an explicit owner
insights.explanation: Rather than bypassing the host gate or rewriting the exporter, the new workstream makes the exact source-attestation exception independently testable and reviewable. This is a more controlled route to releasing the existing preserved review.

insights.title: Queue authority is a separate gate
insights.explanation: A packet can appear as ready/auto in GitHub while CI rejects its queue authority. The failed validation and subsequent handoff must be reconciled before interpreting the pair as executable.

article.takeaway: A concrete recovery pair is published, but the original exporter review remains blocked and the new pair's queue validity is not established.
article.next_watch: Watch for the queue-authority and handoff failures to be resolved, followed by an actual attestation implementation and independently accepted PASS.

stories.headline: WIRE's observation exporter lands; independent review stalls at an attestation gate
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN landed the local sanitized observation exporter and published its private-transport packet pair. The exporter passed reported focused tests, but its independent reviewer stopped at a source-attestation gate before launch. Dropbox transport remains unimplemented and dependency-blocked; a separate repository-validation run failed queue-authority checks.
stories.body:
The local WIRE observation exporter landed on main at 38545e4c12b848861284d77c299790c046df6f62. It consumes a pre-existing task-administrator snapshot, checks evidence completeness and freshness, and preserves unavailable counts rather than manufacturing zeroes. The executor reported 15 focused synthetic tests and changed-file validation passing; GitHub repository validation also passed at the landing SHA. The implementation packet was archived, but implementation testing is not independent acceptance.

The paired review was reportedly claimed as codex-reviewer and stopped by host validation before reviewer launch: 'changed validation manifest is not covered by an accepted exact source attestation.' The preserved review runs and retained worktree are host-reported, not independently inspected here. No independent PASS is established. The private transport implementation/review pair was then published and promoted on main at 8bc0fe40184dec741ccc5a92997052f96e0deb43, with implementation dependent on accepted exporter review. No private observation upload, ChatGPT retrieval, or producer schedule is established.

GitHub Actions additionally show a failed repository validation on the transport authoring commit 8967187af, specifically the task-packet queue-authority step; the automatic authoring handoff succeeded. The Godot Level Pipeline failed at the exporter landing SHA in a separate authored-level lifecycle step. These failures need separate diagnosis; neither proves the exporter itself failed.

Repository queue-authority validation failed on transport authoring commit; investigate separately.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has the first working piece of its operational reporting pipeline: a local exporter that turns an existing task-administrator snapshot into a constrained, sanitized observation. The code has landed, but a separate evidence-authentication rule stopped its independent reviewer before review could begin. The private Dropbox delivery layer must wait.

sections.heading: What the exporter changes
sections.text: Instead of inferring project activity from GitHub branches, the exporter is designed to consume an existing operational snapshot and report only supported counts. It rejects stale or inconsistent evidence and keeps missing values unknown. That is the foundation for a more truthful WIRE status panel, but it is not a live telemetry service yet.

sections.heading: Why the review cannot proceed
sections.text: The reviewer was stopped by a host-validation requirement for an accepted exact source attestation covering the changed validation manifest. Passing implementation tests cannot substitute for this proof. The preserved claim and review evidence need a supported recovery, not a bypass.

sections.heading: Transport is queued, not operating
sections.text: A separate implementation and independent-review pair for private Dropbox delivery has been promoted. Its implementation explicitly depends on accepted exporter review. No upload or ChatGPT readback has been verified. Separately, a repository validation run failed a packet queue-authority check on the transport authoring commit; that failure should be diagnosed rather than conflated with exporter test results.

insights.title: The bottleneck has shifted from code to provenance
insights.explanation: The exporter has landed and reported tests pass. The immediate obstacle is proving the exact reviewed source and validation policy to the independent review system. Resolving that gate unlocks the transport dependency without weakening the acceptance contract.

insights.title: A ready packet is not an active data pipeline
insights.explanation: The transport pair exists in the queue, but its dependency is unmet and there is no verified upload, consumer retrieval, or schedule. WIRE must continue labeling GitHub-only observations as partial.

article.takeaway: The exporter is landed, but the independent-review and private-delivery milestones remain open. Treat the source-attestation recovery as the next gate.
article.next_watch: Watch for a supported source-attestation recovery plan and genuine independent PASS, plus a separate diagnosis of the queue-authority CI failure.

stories.headline: Sepulcher's second recovery queue is withdrawn, leaving its held review unresolved
stories.summary: A second Sepulcher V2 recovery packet pair has been removed from main after its owner withdrew it. The branch's original source and historical corrections were preserved in the archive record. Repository validation passed, but the original independent review remains unresolved and host-local cleanup is unverified.
stories.body: A separate Sepulcher V2 host-validation recovery proposal was administratively withdrawn on November 1. The change removes its implementation and paired-review packets from the active queue and reconciles the indexes, while preserving the original branch head and correction evidence in the branch archive. This is distinct from the earlier source-salvage packet rollback. It does not fix the reported spawn/reset smoke failure or authenticate the original held review. The repository validation for this commit passed. Next, the responsible owner should reconcile the preserved held-review evidence and select a bounded authorized recovery path; host-local worktree and lock disposition remain unknown.

article.lead: Sepulcher's attempt to repair a blocked validation and review path has lost another proposed recovery queue. The owner withdrew the host-validation implementation and review packets, but preserved their historical branch evidence. That keeps the evidence intact while leaving the original review unresolved.

sections.heading: A second withdrawal, not a gameplay rollback
sections.text: The latest commit removes a different recovery pair from the source-salvage proposal withdrawn earlier. This one targeted a reported spawn/reset test regression and a possible failed-report authentication issue. The commit changes task packets, indexes and the branch archive, not the playable scene.

sections.heading: Evidence preserved; acceptance still open
sections.text: The branch archive records the original recovery head and historical corrections. It explicitly does not assert an independent review PASS. The latest repository validation passed, but that checks the withdrawal commit, not the unresolved gameplay smoke or held-review acceptance.

insights.title: Removing a queue item does not close its underlying obligation
insights.explanation: The packet removal reduces the active administrative surface without demonstrating that the failed validation or held-review evidence was resolved. Any future recovery must begin from the preserved evidence rather than interpreting the clean queue as a clean review.

insights.title: The archive is now the continuity point
insights.explanation: By preserving the branch head and historical corrections, the project retains a bounded reference for a future recovery decision. Local worktree and lock cleanup still require host evidence.

article.takeaway: The second Sepulcher recovery proposal is withdrawn, with source history preserved but the original review still unresolved.
article.next_watch: Look for a documented owner decision on the held review, a targeted verified correction, and independently evidenced acceptance or teardown.

At 16:06 UTC, a revert removed both unclaimed packets and restored the prior file index. The rollback's repository validation and authoring workflow succeeded. This is a correction to task authoring, not a gameplay fix, a recovered validation run, or a completed independent review. The next owner should examine the failed handoff and existing recovery authority before proposing a replacement; the original correction branch and reviewer evidence were preserved according to the revert commit. WIRE exporter packets remain ready/auto, but neither their implementation nor transport is verified as landed.

sections.heading: Why the recovery proposal disappeared
sections.text: The proposal sought a bounded way to salvage source evidence for an existing Sepulcher V2 validation problem. The automatic handoff did not accept the pair. A follow-up commit removed both packets and restored the previous file index, rather than leaving an unusable new workstream in the queue.

sections.heading: What the rollback does, and doesn't, establish
sections.text: The rollback passed repository validation and the automatic handoff workflow. Its commit says the original correction branch and reviewer evidence were preserved. That is evidence of a clean repository-level withdrawal, not proof that the underlying scene validation passed or that any host worktree was retired.

insights.title: A failed authoring gate is not a failed game build

insights.explanation: Because the revert explicitly preserves the earlier correction branch and reviewer evidence, the next attempt should reconcile those existing materials before creating a replacement packet.

article.takeaway: The unclaimed salvage proposal was removed from main; Sepulcher V2 recovery still needs an authorized, evidence-backed path.

stories.headline: WIRE telemetry gets an authorized path: exporter and independent-review packets enter the queue
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN has published and automatically promoted a paired implementation and independent-review plan for a read-only WIRE observation exporter. Repository validation and authoring handoff passed. The exporter has not been implemented or claimed; its reviewer must wait until implementation lands.
stories.body: Two agent-ops packets landed on main at 73070fd8 and were promoted to ready/auto at f38d7f40. The implementation packet specifies a local, sanitized, deterministic JSON exporter that consumes an existing task-administrator snapshot without triggering another expensive audit. Its separate review packet requires adversarial checks of freshness, count reconciliation, privacy and read-only behavior. The GitHub authoring and repository validation runs succeeded for the publication commit. Ready/auto is an authoring and dispatch state, not proof of a claim or running implementation. The paired review has an explicit dependency on the implementation landing and archiving. The next gate is a fresh canonical dispatcher eligibility check followed by a separately authorized claim. Dropbox delivery, hourly WIRE integration and public feed changes are outside this implementation packet.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has opened a controlled route to more trustworthy WIRE reporting. A new implementation packet and its independent-review partner have passed authoring validation and entered the dispatch queue. The planned exporter will turn an existing local observation into a sanitized, countable record, without starting another expensive dispatcher audit. No exporter code has landed yet.

sections.heading: The reporting gap is now a defined workstream
sections.text: WIRE can publish project news, but its packet totals are only as trustworthy as the evidence it can actually inspect. The new exporter is designed to preserve the original observation's scope, timestamps and source revision, then reconcile packet counts against a complete sanitized inventory. Missing evidence must remain unknown rather than becoming a misleading zero.

sections.heading: The first milestone is intentionally narrow
sections.text: The implementation is limited to local JSON generation and synthetic tests. It cannot collect new audits, upload to Dropbox, alter claims or change the public feed. A separate reviewer must challenge stale inputs, duplicated identities, privacy leaks and fabricated statuses before the result can be accepted.

sections.heading: Ready to dispatch is not running
sections.text: Both packets are marked ready/auto, but the reviewer depends on a landed, archived implementation. A successful authoring workflow proves that the packet plan passed its checks, not that the exporter exists or has been independently accepted. The next meaningful evidence will be a canonical claim receipt and, later, an implementation landing.

insights.title: A reusable observation is better than another audit
insights.explanation: The dispatcher audit refreshes Git references and can be slow. Reusing an already collected snapshot separates reporting from expensive operational collection and makes the freshness boundary explicit.

insights.title: Privacy and accuracy share one review gate
insights.explanation: The exporter will summarize authority-bearing queue evidence while crossing a public-reporting boundary. Its independent review is tasked with catching both incorrect counts and sensitive data leakage before downstream integration.

article.takeaway: The reporting improvement is now formally authorized for dispatch, not implemented. Its first deliverable is a local, testable evidence format; publication and private transport come later.
article.next_watch: Look for a verified dispatcher claim for agent-wire-observation-export-v1, then focused validation, landing, and a separate independent-review receipt.

stories.headline: A five-minute test limit is obstructing validator acceptance; a bounded timeout fix enters the queue
stories.summary: A new P0 implementation/review pair was declared ready/auto to increase the canonical paired-review runner test timeout from 300 to 480 seconds. The packet cites a 317.595-second suite runtime, longer than the existing limit. This is a validation-infrastructure correction, not a passing test or accepted security fix.
stories.body: Commit aa7fb473 authored a P0 timeout correction and independent review. Commit f070b4ee changed both headers to ready/auto. The implementation is restricted to the paired_review_runner_unit timeout, leaving the test command and other limits unchanged. The 317.595-second runtime is reported in the packet, not independently reproduced in this monitoring run. Latest checked CI runs for aa7fb473 passed repository validation and automatic handoff; they do not demonstrate that the long runner suite passed. Implementation, independent PASS, executor liveness and teardown remain unverified.

article.lead: A test that takes longer than its permitted runtime cannot produce the green evidence needed to accept a security-sensitive repair. CUSTODIAN has now prepared a narrow correction: give one canonical paired-review suite more time without changing what it tests.

sections.heading: The bottleneck is the clock
sections.text: The new packet reports that the paired-review runner suite took 317.595 seconds while its validation manifest allows 300. That mismatch can terminate a genuine run before it can produce an acceptable report. The number comes from the packet, not a fresh host measurement.

sections.heading: A narrow fix, still awaiting execution
sections.text: The proposed change raises only paired_review_runner_unit's limit to 480 seconds. Both implementation and independent-review packets are now declared ready/auto, but the review cannot proceed until the implementation lands and passes validation.

insights.title: A timeout failure is not a product failure
insights.explanation: A run cut short by its budget does not establish whether the validator is correct. Fixing the budget restores the opportunity to obtain trustworthy evidence; it does not itself prove the validator safe.

insights.title: Green repository CI is not the missing test
insights.explanation: Repository validation passed for the authoring commit, but that is distinct from an authenticated completed run of the long paired-review suite.

article.takeaway: The next useful milestone is a completed canonical runner report against the unchanged test command, followed by independent review.
article.next_watch: Watch for a landed single-value timeout change, a completed suite report, and an independent PASS; none is established yet.

stories.headline: New safeguard targets the validation loophole left by cycle 2
stories.summary: A new implementation and independent-review pair has been promoted to ready/auto to close the mismatch between after-sync validation evidence produced during changed-main merges and the host validator that consumes it. The historical cycle-2 human_required outcome remains unchanged. Dispatch, implementation, acceptance and teardown are unverified.
stories.body: The archived cycle-2 reviewer identified R2-01: the producer requires after-sync validation witnesses for changed-main merges, but the paired-review host consumer does not authenticate those witnesses. Commit 956a272 creates a bounded correction and independent-review pair; commit 7a6dfdf changes both packet headers to ready/auto. The review depends on the implementation landing and normal teardown. No claim, execution, accepted PASS or host cleanup is established by these commits. This is a prospective fix, not retroactive acceptance of the historical human_required review.
bullets: Two named packets promoted from draft/manual to ready/auto.

Fresh independent review is dependency-gated; original cycle-2 human_required remains unchanged.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has prepared a targeted repair for a gap in its independent-review safety checks. The system that produces validation evidence requires proof after merging newer main-branch code, but the system that checks the merge does not yet demand that same proof. A new implementation and review pair is ready for dispatch, not yet completed.

sections.heading: A mismatch at the trust boundary
sections.text: The producer already requires validation after a changed-main synchronization. The host validator can still authenticate that synchronization without consuming the corresponding validation witness. This creates a route for unvalidated source to appear adequately checked.

sections.heading: A prospective repair with an independent gate
sections.text: The new packet calls for real-Git failing-first reproduction, exact witness binding, negative tests for missing or reused evidence, and preservation of supported workflows. A separate fresh-context reviewer must test the result after implementation lands.

sections.heading: The historical finding stays intact
sections.text: The original cycle-2 review remains human_required. This work cannot rewrite its evidence or convert that past result into PASS. The new pair is declared ready/auto, but dispatch, execution, acceptance and cleanup have not been observed.

insights.title: The missing check is on the receiving side
insights.explanation: The producer and consumer enforce different evidence contracts. Fixing only the producer would not prevent the host validator from accepting a merge without checking the required witness.

insights.title: Ready is not accepted
insights.explanation: Both packets are marked ready/auto, but the reviewer is dependency-gated behind implementation. The safety improvement remains hypothetical until independently tested and accepted.

article.takeaway: A narrowly scoped prospective correction is ready for dispatch; no implementation landing or independent PASS has been established.
article.next_watch: Look for a real-Git failing-first reproduction, source landing, fresh independent review receipt and verified canonical teardown.

stories.headline: Sepulcher's paving preview lands, but its independent review hits a source-evidence gate
stories.summary: A playable Godot preview now includes four native-resolution paving crops, the real Operator and camera, and three comparison modes. The implementation was landed and archived, but its independent review has no verdict: a source-scope host check rejected four paths. A narrowly pinned recovery proposal is drafted, not approved or dispatched.
stories.body: The Sepulcher paving experiment advanced from instructions to a committed, playable comparison scene. The scene uses four 512-pixel crops, the real Operator and camera, and neutral, full-crop and deliberate repeat presentations. The implementation closeout reports Godot, crop, LFS and capture checks passed, and the task packet was archived. That is implementation progress, not independent review acceptance or production-art approval. The preserved independent review received no verdict after its pre-review host source-scope check rejected four paths missing from the historical task's explicit source list. A new source-scope attestation implementation/review pair is drafted/manual. It proposes an exact four-path exception that cannot activate before its own independently accepted PASS, then separate recovery of the original preserved review run. Host worktree and liveness status are not independently verified.

article.lead: Sepulcher Gardens now has a committed playable paving comparison, bringing its first experimental floor material into a real Operator-camera scene. But the technical review has stopped before a verdict because the historical task did not explicitly name four source paths.

sections.heading: From artwork to a playable comparison
sections.text: The new Godot scene places four native 512-pixel crops alongside a neutral floor and a deliberately repeated tile. Switching modes lets reviewers distinguish the quality of the original composition from visible repetition in gameplay.

sections.heading: Why the review stopped
sections.text: The implementation was landed and archived, with tests reported in its closeout. Its separate independent review was preserved without a verdict when a host check rejected four source-bearing paths outside the original packet's explicit scope. No PASS or art approval follows from the implementation landing.

sections.heading: A narrow recovery, not a shortcut
sections.text: A new draft/manual attestation pair proposes pinning exactly those four historical paths. Its exception would remain inactive until its own independent review earns canonical acceptance. Only then could the original preserved review be recovered separately.

insights.title: A playable scene is not an accepted asset
insights.explanation: The preview now exists in code, but neither its independent technical review nor the human visual approval has been completed. That separation protects the production asset pipeline.

insights.title: Review provenance is the new bottleneck
insights.explanation: The blocker is not a missing texture or game scene. It is the review system's inability to authenticate four historically omitted source paths without weakening its broader protections.

article.takeaway: Sepulcher's preview implementation landed; independent technical acceptance and production-art approval remain outstanding.
article.next_watch: Look for a properly authorized, independently accepted four-path attestation and then recovery of the original preserved review.

stories.headline: Validator's second correction closes without a passing independent review
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN's cycle-2 paired-review validator correction was archived with a nonpassing review outcome. This is a documented closeout, not acceptance of the validator fix. Further remediation requires an explicit decision rather than treating the completed packet as a PASS.
stories.body: A new main-branch closeout commit records a nonpassing independent review for the second validator correction and archives the correction packet. The distinction matters: completing or archiving an implementation does not mean the independent reviewer accepted its safety behavior. The previous review had identified a retry path that could bypass validation evidence. The latest closeout does not establish that the flaw is resolved or the review accepted. The next action is to inspect the exact findings and decide on bounded human-directed remediation; no automatic third correction is implied.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's second attempt to repair a validator loophole has reached closeout, but not acceptance. The latest record explicitly calls the independent review nonpassing, keeping the safety gate unresolved.

sections.heading: Closeout does not mean approval
sections.text: The correction packet has been archived. The paired independent review did not produce an accepted PASS, so the archive cannot be interpreted as evidence that the retry-path defect is fixed.

sections.heading: The decision moves back to the findings
sections.text: The prior review showed that retrying after synchronization could bypass required validation evidence. The exact latest findings must be inspected before choosing another bounded repair; a third automatic correction should not be assumed.

stories.headline: A second review catches a retry loophole in CUSTODIAN's safety gate
stories.summary: An independent review of the first validator correction found R1-01: a retry could land code after a main-branch merge without consuming a required after-sync validation report. The finding is recorded and a second correction/review pair is declared ready/auto. No cycle-2 implementation or PASS is established.
stories.body: The first correction improved the source-sync witness checks, but its independent reviewer reproduced a separate bypass: a finish attempt synchronizes main and pauses for validation, then a retry with an invalid report can land when the next sync returns unchanged. Cycle-1 review outcome is findings, not acceptance. Two new cycle-2 packets declare ready/auto, each with sequential prerequisites. Canonical dispatch, execution, passing review, and host teardown are unverified.
bullets: Cycle-1 independent review reproduced the invalid after-sync retry bypass R1-01.
Cycle-2 correction and paired review declare ready/auto; dispatch and acceptance are not proven.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's review safeguards have uncovered a second flaw while trying to close the first. A reviewer showed that a retry could slip past validation after synchronizing with newer main-branch code, so the previous correction has findings rather than independent acceptance.

sections.heading: The dangerous second attempt
sections.text: The first finish attempt correctly pauses after merging newer main code. On retry, however, the merge is no longer new. The existing implementation checks the required validation report only when that invocation sees a changed merge. The reviewer reproduced a finish that accepted a false report by never examining it.

sections.heading: A second correction is prepared
sections.text: The archived cycle-1 review preserves finding R1-01. A new implementation packet and a separate independent-review packet are now declared ready for automatic handoff. They are sequential, not evidence that the repair is already running or accepted.

insights.title: A green test suite did not cover the retry
insights.explanation: The review's selected validation checks passed, but the missing retry scenario still allowed an invalid finish. This is a concrete gap between passing tests and a trustworthy lifecycle gate.

insights.title: The next fix must remember what happened before retry
insights.explanation: The new packet requires the pending synchronized tree and its validation report to remain bound across retries, including when the latest synchronization reports no change.

article.takeaway: The original provenance correction is not independently accepted; a second, narrower correction is ready to address the newly reproduced bypass.
article.next_watch: Look for the cycle-2 implementation landing, a regression proving invalid retries fail, and an independent PASS receipt.
